system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Package Against Buyer Playbook

**Preliminary note:** The seller's cover note asks us to treat [STANDARD] clauses as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to focus only on [OPEN] items. I have not done that. Nothing in the package shows agreement from our side, and almost every [STANDARD] item departs from our playbook. The cover note is also the other side's characterisation, so I've reviewed all items. I have only the seller's summary, not the full SPA, so clause cross-references should be checked against the actual draft.

## Material Departures and Reasoning

**1. General warranty cap (Cl 12.1): AUD 4.8m / 20%**
Our opening position is 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% figure is only a conditional fallback, and it requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given, so we cannot accept it. Counter at AUD 6.0m.

**2. Thresholds (Cl 12.2): AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k basket, excess-only recovery**
This is five times our de minimis (AUD 5k) and five times our basket (AUD 50k). The excess-only structure is a deductible, not a first-dollar basket. Under our position, once AUD 50k is exceeded the seller is liable from the first dollar. Counter at AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first dollar.

**3. Time limits (Cl 12.3/13): 18 months, plus a "universal limitation" sweep**
Our general claims period is 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which we don't have. The sweep clause, under which any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise, is a hidden general-regime override. It would pull title, tax, IP and fraud claims into the general regime, which the playbook prohibits. Counter at 24 months and delete the sweep.

**4. Fundamental/Title claims: subject to general caps and time limits**
This is the most serious departure. Our playbook requires a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. The seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify it. Title and capacity go to the heart of what we are buying, and the seller's own DD-012 reliance (see point 13) shows why independent evidence matters. Reject outright.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
This would bar fraud and deliberate misconduct claims. Our position carves fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this. Reject, and make the carve-out non-waivable.

**6. Disclosure: whole data room, Accounts and public registers (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2)**
Deemed disclosure of the entire data room and public registers is exactly what the playbook rejects. It would put the burden on us to find issues in roughly the whole data room and then deem them disclosed. The seller's own letter (DL 1.1) cross-refers to "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room, which is far broader than specific disclosure. Require specific, fair disclosure against each warranty. Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures, and reject DL 11 to the extent it asks us to evaluate against the "complete agreement and current due diligence record" as a basis for limiting claims.

**7. Buyer knowledge (Cl 8.3): no claim for matters the buyer or its advisers knew or could discover**
This is a blanket buyer-knowledge bar, combined with a deemed data-room and public-records standard. Our playbook deletes it. Any knowledge qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and it must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Reject. Note that this interacts with point 6: together they would defeat most claims on matters in the data room.

**8. Bluefen consent (Cl 3/6.3): reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery**
Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue, and the disclosure letter confirms no final written consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent. "Satisfied on delivery" would let us be bound before the consent is effective. Require effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Failure should give us a walk-away right, not a post-completion remedy.

**9. Riverlark facility (Cl 2/7): AUD 3.2m, to be "addressed by a release following Completion"**
This is financial debt. Under a debt-free/cash-free structure it should be deducted at Completion. The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. The disclosure confirms the facility is unpaid and security has not been discharged. Reject. Require a payoff letter and direct repayment at Completion.

**10. Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DL 5): AUD 420k excluded as "a matter for the Seller"**
The bonuses are not in the Completion funds flow, and the disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. Our playbook requires either a specific line item or seller funding, including triggered on-costs, and forbids a silent exclusion. The seller's phrasing is a silent exclusion. Require the bonuses and on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded, and check the funds flow against the full DD-005 list.

**11. Ironquay IP (Cl 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "adequate"**
Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 project materials transfer only on payment of every SOW3 fee. DL 4 records no receipt or confirmatory assignment, so IP title is unresolved. The AUD 180k figure in DD-010 is not independent bank verification either way, so we should neither accept nor dispute it on that basis. Playbook requires broadening the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure (payment and confirmatory assignment). Counter with a broader indemnity covering failure of IP transfer, third-party claims and unpaid fees generally, with the cure preserved.

**12. Export/privacy incident DD-006 (Cl 4.6/Sch 6): "preliminary, not expected to be material"**
The disclosure says the investigation is preliminary and does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the scope (~1,240 records) or whether notification is required. Per the playbook, we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way. We should not accept "not expected to be material" as a settled characterisation in the SPA. Require preservation of logs, a completed investigation, and regular updates. My suggestion, beyond the playbook and subject to principal sign-off, is a specific indemnity covering notification and regulatory costs if a notifiable event later arises.

**13. Title (DL 10 / "evidenced by DD-012"): share register as proof of title**
DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent evidence. Playbook requires independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances (for example, PPSR and ASIC searches) and authority. Title warranties also belong in the fundamental regime (point 4). Reject DD-012 as sufficient proof.

**14. Sandbar renewals (DL 8): AUD 330k "ordinary course operating costs"**
The disclosure itself says it is unknown whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The playbook requires assessment, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Reject the seller's characterisation until supported. Request the contracts and check DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing and scope overlap, in case the three renewals are double-counted or split.

**15. Tax and IP (Seller update): "settled under the general regime"**
This is wrong. Our playbook keeps tax and IP open, with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution. Keep these as separate categories and reject any suggestion they are settled under the general regime (also see point 3).

**16. Items not in the playbook: Mossvale (DL 9) and office lease (DL 7)**
Both disclosures describe assignment or notification provisions without confirming whether consent is required for the share sale. The playbook does not address these directly. Request written confirmation from the seller on whether consent or notice is required and, if so, add it to the conditions or the funds flow as appropriate.

## Summary of Recommendations

**Reject outright:**
- Fundamental/Title claims in the general regime (point 4)
- Universal limitation sweep (point 3)
- Carve-out removal for fraud and deliberate misconduct (point 5)
- Whole-data-room, public-register and Accounts deemed disclosure (point 6)
- Blanket buyer-knowledge bar (point 7)
- Consent-on-delivery for Bluefen (point 8)
- Post-completion Riverlark release without undertaking and approval (point 9)
- Silent exclusion of the AUD 420k bonuses (point 10)
- Tax and IP "settled" position (point 15)
- DD-012 as proof of title (point 13)

**Counter-propose:**
- General cap: AUD 6.0m / 25% (point 1)
- De minimis AUD 5k, basket AUD 50k, first-dollar recovery (point 2)
- General claims period: 24 months (point 3)
- Fundamental/Title: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar (point 4)
- Specific fair disclosure only (point 6)
- Knowledge qualifiers limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, never excusing title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities (point 7)
- Bluefen: effective consent and evidence of conditions as a pre-Completion condition (point 8)
- Riverlark: payoff letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases (point 9)
- Bonuses and on-costs as a specific funds-flow line or seller-funded (point 10)
- Broadened Ironquay indemnity with SOW3 cure preserved; independent verification of the AUD 180k (point 11)
- DD-006: log preservation, completed investigation, regular updates; consider a specific indemnity (point 12)
- Sandbar: contract review and assessment, no automatic price deduction (point 14)

**Information requests:**
- Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence (point 13)
- Confirmation on Mossvale and office lease consent requirements (point 16)
- Bank evidence on the Ironquay SOW3 payments (point 11)
- Sandbar contracts and DD-008/DD-011 reconciliation (point 14)

**Approvals required before any fallback is offered:**
- 20% / AUD 4.8m cap, 18-month period, or Riverlark post-completion release: each needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. None has been given, so none should be offered in the mark-up.
=== END ADVICE ===
